title: Why top investors secretly love YC: read incentives and judge investors by what they do, not say
summary: Dalton and Michael Seibel explain the gap between investors dismissing YC publicly and funding YC companies constantly. The lesson for founders: understand each investor's incentives (first check, ownership, price) and weigh actions over talk.

principles.text: Investors say 'too early' when a startup lacks signal; a credible filter like YC supplies that signal.
principles.quote: too early just means there's not enough signal that this is one of these epic standout companies which is their job to invest in

principles.text: Packaged, pre-filtered deal flow is valuable to investors because they can only do so many deals.
principles.quote: the average VC only does one deal a year maybe two deals a year

principles.text: Investors want to be your first check and dislike you talking to many investors in parallel; talk to many anyway.
principles.quote: it's scary when your customers first talk to someone else before you because you can get disintermediated in the future

principles.text: Seed funds want big ownership at low prices, so they have a built-in incentive to discourage you from doing YC.
principles.quote: your job is to get a big ownership in the company and then try to get the VCS to fund them in the next round

principles.text: Understand the incentives of whoever is marketing or advising you; they are running a business too.
principles.quote: the people who are marketing to you are running their businesses and those businesses have Dynamics you understand those Dynamics

principles.text: Discount advice from investors who aren't offering money; take real offers seriously and judge by actions, not tweets.
principles.quote: maybe you should spend a little bit more time looking at what people do rather than what they say or they meme or they tweet
